## 2.4.2.1.4. Guidance, Forms and Work Instrvctions:

- Guidance, forms and work instructions may be needed to supplement project procedures. Where
- Anumberof formsand templateswill bemandatedfor usebyEimaarMisr inorder to standardize information and achieve consistency of data. Details of these documents will be communicated separately and asrequired to thoseProgramPartners whorequire to use them.

## 2.4.2.2. Legal Compliance

- >AfundamentalrequirementofforallworksontheEMAARMisrProgramis that theyareundertaken in compliance with the requirements of relevant legislation and standards.ProgramPartners shall to ensure that they are familiar with, and keep up to date on developments associated with, the Program Partners shall providc propcr and lawful access to Regulatory enforcement staff and other related parties suchasrepresentatives ofinsurers.ProgramPartners shallensure thatEMAARMisr are immediately advised of all action byRegulators in connectionwith theWorks,including:
- Sitcvisits and comments made during such visits.
- Siteinspections and commentsmadeduringsuchinspections.
- Writtencommunication.
- Enforcementnoticesorotherformal action.

## 2.4.2.3.Planning and Controls

- >All work activities are to be suitably planned and implemented. Planning is vital to ensure work activities are adequately controlled and thehealth and safety risks to personnel are reduced to as low as reasonably practicable.This can only be achieved through coordinated action by everyone who expects to put people towork.
- Effective planning will include compliance to the health and safety management system and the relevant plans and procedures.

## 2.4.2.3.1.Risk Asscssment:

- Risk assessment is one ofthe most important activities when planning the work and if done properly will make a significant contribution towards the reduction of accidents and ill health.
- All work activities shall have'suitable and sufficient'risk assessments are carried out,recorded and briefed to relevant groups or personnel prior to the onset of the works.
- For a risk assessment to be suitable and sufficient it must:
- Establish the hazards and associated risks arisingfrom thework activity.
- Be appropriate, given the nature of the work, and such that it remains valid for a reasonable period of time.
- Beproportionateto thelevel of riskand thenatureof thework.
